children: Oct 22 (Reuters) – Large investment managers bought $28.956 billion at a 10-year note auction held in October,compared with the $25.872 billion they purchased the previous month, data from the U.S. Treasury Department released on Thursday showed.

Overseas investors, another major group of holders of U.S. government debt, bought $8.214 billion of the latest 10-year supply,compared with $10.959 billion they purchased the previous month, according to the Treasury Department’s auction allotment data.
The Treasury also sold some of $40 billion of 10-year notes earlier this month to banks, pension funds and Wall Street bond dealers.

At other auctions held the same week as the 10-year auction, large investment managers bought $45.499 billion of 3-year notes,compared with the $43.063 billion they purchased the previous month. They bought $14.572 billion in 30-year bonds versus $12.001 billionthe prior month.

Overseas investors bought $5.068 billion of the latest 3-year supply, compared with $7.056 billion they purchased the previous month.They bought $5.488 billion of 30-year bonds versus $9.307 billion the prior month.
The Treasury offered $59 billion in 3-year notes and $23 billion in 30-year bonds.
